entries.etymology: Sax. self, sylf; Goth. silba; Sw. sielf; Dan. selv; G. selbst; D. zelf.
senses: In old authors, this word sometimes signifies particular, very, or same.
In present usage, self is united to certain personal pronouns and pronominal adjectives, to express emphasis or distinction; also when the pronoun is used reciprocally; as, I myself.
Self is sometimes used as a noun, noting the individual subject to his own contemplation or action, or noting identity of person. Consciousness makes every one to be what he calls self.
It also signifies personal interest, or love of private interest; selfishness. Self is much used in composition.

entries.etymology: Sax. sunna; Goth. sunno; G. sonne; D. zon.
senses: The splendid orb or luminary which, being in or near the centre of our system of worlds, gives light and heat to all the planets.
In popular usage, a sunny place; a place where the beams of the sun fall.
Any thing eminently splendid or luminous; that which is the chief source of light or honor.
In Scripture, Christ is called the Sun of righteousness, as the source of light, animation and comfort to his disciples.
The luminary or orb which constitutes the centre of any system of worlds. -- Under the sun: in the world; on earth; a proverbial expression.

entries.etymology: Sax. woruld, weruld; D. waereld; Sw. verld.
senses: The universe; the whole system of created globes and vast bodies of matter.
The earth; the terraqueous globe.
The heavens.
System of beings; or the orbs which occupy space, and all the beings which inhabit them. Heb. xi.
Present state of existence.
A secular life.
Public life; or society.
Business or trouble of life.
A great multitude or quantity.
Mankind; people in general; in an indefinite sense.
Course of life.
Universal empire.
The customs and manners of men; the practice of life.
All the world contains.
The principal nations or countries of the earth.
The Roman empire. Scripture.
A large tract of country; a wide compass of things.
The inhabitants of the earth; the whole human race. John iii.
The carnal state or corruption of the earth. Gal. i.
The ungodly part of the world.
Time; as in the phrase, world without end.
A collection of wonders; [obs.] -- In the world: in possibility. -- For all the world: (1) Exactly; [little used.] Sidney. (2) For any consideration.

entries.etymology: ME < AFr < Late L. potēre, to be able.
senses: Ability; capacity; capability; skill; aptitude.
Strength; might; stamina; endurance; fortitude; [fig.] will; courage; heart; spirit; determination.
Influence; ability to affect; capacity to impact.
Force; violence; aggression.
Fuel; energy source.
Life force; potential to live, die, and resurrect from the dead.
[Fig.] God; omnipotent being; supremely divine entity.
[Fig.] Satan; tempter; deceiver; temptation; enticement.
[Fig.] means; way; method; process.
